claim_ceiling: Source-authored finite-spin equatorial prograde Kerr scattering-deflection quadrature and independent 20-case equation-level SciPy comparison grid. The exact-head Rust workflow must pass before calling the numerical solver validated. This does not reproduce the paper's pinned 55-trajectory matched-NLO study, provide an image-branch catalogue/caustic map, or implement wave optics. The cited 2026 result is an arXiv preprint, not assumed peer-reviewed.

reference.title: Uniform Strong-Deflection Lensing in Near-Extremal Kerr
reference.author: Shakibul Chowdhury
reference.reported_validation: Matched next-to-leading-order correction is compared against high-precision integrations for 55 trajectories; the paper reports improvement for all 55.
reference.reported_branch_result: Near-extremal image-branch accumulation crosses between algebraic and exponential behaviour, with crossover order scaling as kappa^-1; the high-order extremal-like coordinate-time spacing approaches 4*pi*M.

conventions.units: G=c=M=1 for dimensionless formulas; dimensional scale restored with M where noted
conventions.spin: a = dimensionless Kerr spin a_phys/M, restricted to 0 <= a <= 1 for prograde equatorial branch

properties: Rescale r/M=1+kappa*y before evaluating near-horizon radial potential, avoiding direct subtraction of O(1) terms that leaves O(kappa^2) residuals.
Use the depressed-cubic radial potential factorization to bracket the outer turning point from the radial-potential minimum.
Use a compact coordinate with finite analytic limits at both the square-root turning point and infinity.
Report the leading uniform phase as an asymptotic comparison only; it is not substituted for the finite-spin numerical integral.
Reject exact extremality in the finite-kappa routine; the exactly extremal normal form is a separate method.
tests_authored: exact extremal a=1 gives r_ph/M=1 and b_c/M=2
near-extremal (b_c/M-2)/kappa converges monotonically toward sqrt(3) across kappa={0.1,0.03,0.01,0.003,0.001}
scaled-offset impact parameter, equatorial Q=0 constants, and leading phase identity
negative spin branch, nonpositive/nonfinite chi and extremal scaled-offset misuse are rejected
implementation.limitation: The Rust numerical quadrature implements finite-spin equatorial prograde scattering and is compared to independent SciPy equation-level reference values. It does not yet reproduce the paper's matched-NLO formula or its exact 55 trajectory catalogue.

numerical_method.scaled_radial_potential: R/kappa^2 evaluated from P/kappa and y^2-1, with P/kappa reconstructed relative to the analytic critical orbit.
numerical_method.outer_turning_point: Use the local minimum r_min=sqrt((b^2-a^2)/3) of the equatorial radial-potential cubic as the left bracket; bracket and bisect the outer scattering root to avoid mistaking the inner branch or photon-orbit-radius sign for the outer turning point.
numerical_method.integral: Delta phi = 2*integral_(r_turn)^infinity [(b-a)+a*P/Delta]/sqrt(R) dr; compactify y=y_turn+S*x^2/(1-x^2), x in [0,1], with analytic endpoint limits.
numerical_method.quadrature: Adaptive Simpson with explicit relative/absolute tolerances, recursion-depth and evaluation budgets.

high_value_numerical_benchmark.goal: After the finite-spin quadrature passes NEK-20, reproduce the paper's 55 high-precision subextremal/near-extremal prograde equatorial scattering trajectories after pinning arXiv version, NLO expression, exact trajectory inputs and all coordinate conventions.
required_comparison: exact Kerr radial-potential turning point and high-precision quadrature/reference trajectory
paper's matched next-to-leading-order uniform asymptotic phase
report_per_trajectory: integration tolerance, step/refinement history and runtime

acceptance.asymptotic_convergence: For each fixed chi>0, kappa*Phi_numeric must converge toward ln(1+2*sqrt(3)/chi) as kappa decreases; estimate and report the observed order instead of imposing an unmeasured universal rate.
acceptance.matched_NLO: Must improve aggregate phase error against the leading formula on the pinned 55-trajectory set; report all individual cases and any exceptions.

high_value_numerical_benchmark.claim_ceiling: The 20-case SciPy grid is not a reproduction of the paper's 55 trajectories. The paper's matched-NLO expression must be transcribed from a pinned version before the NLO comparison can be claimed.

image_branch_and_timing_target.status: future cross-check; image-branch continuation and timing comparison not implemented

negative_controls: use the subextremal logarithmic expansion unchanged at exact extremality
apply the prograde formula to negative-spin or retrograde rays
evaluate the finite-kappa scaled-offset formula at kappa=0
treat the leading crossover phase as an exact finite-spin deflection
claim reproduction of 55 trajectories without pinning the reference version and individual trajectory inputs
compare phase values after mixing affine, Boyer-Lindquist coordinate-time and azimuthal conventions
bracket first positive radial potential value at the photon-orbit radius instead of the outer scattering root
mix the inner radial turning root with the outer scattering root
evaluate R(r) as an unscaled difference of O(1) near-horizon terms
replace the finite-spin deflection integral with the leading uniform asymptotic phase
report a converged integral when the adaptive evaluation/depth budget was exhausted

numerical_reference_grid.reference_method: Independent SciPy adaptive quadrature of the exact equatorial Kerr radial-potential integral using a separately derived turning-point-regular coordinate. Equation-level reference; not a claimed Rust result or the paper's 55-trajectory dataset.

acceptance.finite_spin_deflection_relative_error_ag: <=2e-7 for each of the 20 frozen points
acceptance.quadrature_error: finite, nonnegative, and below the requested tolerance
acceptance.uniform_crossover: For fixed chi=0.5, abs(kappa*deflection-F(chi)) decreases monotonically across kappa={0.1,0.03,0.01,0.003,0.001}; no equality is asserted at finite kappa.
